extra.message: The `username` query parameter from GET /select is interpolated directly into a SQL string via an f-string and passed to `run_sql_query`/`cursor.execute()` with no parameterization or escaping. An attacker can supply e.g. `" OR "1"="1` to dump all users, or use UNION-based/stacked-query payloads to exfiltrate password hashes and other data from the SQLite database.

In PUT /user, the request body fields `user.name`, `user.username`, `user.address`, `user.email`, and `user.contact` are interpolated directly into an INSERT SQL string via f-string formatting and executed with `run_sql_query(query, commit=True)` with no parameterization. A value like `", "x", "x", "x", "x", "x"); DROP TABLE users;--` in any of these fields breaks out of the string literal and injects arbitrary SQL.

POST /find reads an arbitrary JSON object from the request body (`await request.json()`) and passes it unvalidated as a MongoDB-style query filter to `get_nosql_users()`, which calls `db_client.vfapi.users.find(query)`. Because the entire filter is attacker-controlled, an attacker can use query operators (e.g. `{"password": {"$regex": "^5f4"}}`, `{"password": {"$ne": null}}`) to perform blind NoSQL injection and enumerate/extract user records — including password hashes — field-by-field, or use operators like `$where` to alter query logic. The response only strips `password`/`_id` from the returned document after the match is made, so match/no-match behavior alone leaks data character-by-character.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: The `username` query parameter from DELETE /user is interpolated directly into a `DELETE FROM users WHERE username = "{username}"` SQL string with no parameterization, allowing SQL injection (e.g. deleting all rows via `" OR "1"="1`).

In DELETE /user, `user.address` from the request body is interpolated unquoted and unsanitized into `DELETE FROM users WHERE address = {user.address}`, allowing SQL injection through the address field of the User model.

POST /reset has no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated remote user can trigger `remove(f'{DB_FILENAME}.sql.db')` and `rmtree(f'{DB_FILENAME}.nosql.db')`, permanently destroying all stored user data (SQL and NoSQL stores) and forcing regeneration with fresh fake data. This is a critical function exposed with no access control, enabling trivial denial of service / data destruction.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: DELETE /user allows any unauthenticated caller to delete any user account by supplying an arbitrary `username` (or `user.address`) with no ownership check, session validation, or authorization of any kind — a full IDOR/missing-authorization vulnerability enabling mass account deletion.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: User passwords submitted to PUT /user are hashed with MD5 (`md5(user.password.encode()).hexdigest()`) before storage. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted, making stored password hashes trivially crackable via rainbow tables or brute force if the database is ever exposed (e.g. via the SQL/NoSQL injection findings above).

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
